messages.subject: Confusing error output when compiling Nimble distribution
parts:
Dear all,

I am having some trouble when compiling a Nimble distribution I created to analyse detection / nondetection data. Strangely, the function returns a valid value when I pass some data outside of Nimble, but then returns this error when compiling:

Compiling [Note] This may take a minute. [Note] Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details. Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) : cannot load shared object 'C:/Users/jba/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpiEgetg/nimble_generatedCode/P_4_rcFun_R_GlobalEnv7_10_28_13_36_03.dll':
LoadLibrary failure: Access is denied.

See the function I created, some simulated data for reproducibility, and at the end of the message the full C++ output I get at compilation. Any help or suggestion is much appreciated.

###FUNCTION#####
library(nimble)
dmarocc <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), #Detection/nondetection row
                 ivec = double(1), #Vector with the initial state probabilities
                 nint = double(0), #Number of capture intervals, is nyears - 1
                 nstates = double(0), #Number of states
                 FR = double(0), #Vector with the number individuals that share every unique capture history
                 ps = double(3), #State transition matrix
                 po = double(3), #Observation transition matrix
                 log = integer(0, default = 0) #Compulsory argument, 0 for likelihood, 1 for loglikelihood
  ){
   
    returnType(double(0))
   
    zeta <- matrix(value = NA, nrow = nint+1, ncol = nstates)
   
    zeta[1, 1:nstates] <- ivec[1:nstates]*po[1:nstates, x[1], 1]
   
   
    for(t in 1:nint){ 
      for(s in 1:nstates){
     
      zeta[t+1, s]  <- inprod(zeta[t,1:nstates], ps[1:nstates,s,t]) * po[s,x[t+1],t]
     
      }
    }
   
   
    lik <- sum(zeta[nint+1,1:nstates])
    logProb <- FR*log(lik)
   
   
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
  
  })

###SIMULATED DATA######

x <- rep(c(1,2), times = 10)
psi1 <- 0.6
ivec <- c(psi1, 1-psi1)
nint <- length(x) - 1
nstates <- 2
FR <- 1

ps <- po <- array(data = NA, dim = c(nstates,nstates,nint))

gam <- .3
phi <- .8
p <- .95


ps[1,1,] <- phi
ps[1,2,] <- 1-phi
ps[2,1,] <- gam
ps[2,2,] <- 1-gam
po[1,1,] <- p
po[1,2,] <- 1-p
po[2,1,] <- 0
po[2,2,] <- 1

###TEST THE FUNCTION OUTSIDE OF NIMBLE###

dmarocc(x = x, ivec = ivec, nint = nint, nstates = nstates, FR = FR, ps = ps, po = po, log = 1)

#Result:
#[1] -23.92458

###COMPILE THE FUNCTION###

compileNimble(dmarocc, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Confusing error output when compiling Nimble distribution
parts:
Dear Jaume,

Your code runs without problems for me. I can do:

Ctest <- compileNimble(dmarocc)
Ctest(x = x, ivec = ivec, nint = nint, nstates = nstates, FR = FR, ps = ps, po = po, log = 1)
# answer matches: [1] -23.92458

The compiler output has a set of warnings (and these we don't try to silence because doing so could be different on each OS+compiler combination), but I don't see any errors.

It appears the problem is that your system is denying you access to the compiled DLL. The "inDL" is a function defined within the source code for "dyn.load", which is used to load the DLL after nimble has called the C++ compiler on your system. (See here. ) I am wondering if this could possibly have to do with some kind of permissions issue on your system?

Are you able to run a basic nimble example on your system (e.g. from our r-nimble.org examples or from the user manual)?

If you are adventurous and want to stop nimble immediately before it tries to load your DLL, you can do,

nimble:::cppProjectClass$trace(loadSO, browser)

Then compileNimble will stop right at the single line of code in the loadSO method of the cppProjectClass class and (from what you will see) you can enter getSOName() to see exactly where the compiled DLL is on your system (if you don't already know). And you can see the dyn.load call used to load it and can try that manually to explore why you are getting "Access Denied."

For now I checked your code on Mac, not Windows.

HTH
Perry
